\section{Setup}

\texttt{benchmarks/competitors/setup\_xaros.sh} in the sporos repository installs every tool at the version of Table S1, downloads the genomes from NCBI and UCSC, simulates the reads (\texttt{sim\_reads.py}, fixed seeds) and builds the harnesses; \texttt{run\_seeds.sh}, \texttt{run\_lookups.sh}, \texttt{run\_mems.sh}, \texttt{run\_capped.sh} and \texttt{run\_smems.sh} run the benchmarks and write the raw measurements that the main tables are made from. Each timed command ran under \texttt{/usr/bin/time -v} after the machine had kept at most 1.5 processors busy for half a second; wall time is the best of three runs (one for runs past 60~s), memory the largest peak resident set size of those runs. Kernel benchmarks (Table 1, Table 2) time only the computation, inside each tool's own harness.

The commands, with \texttt{R} and \texttt{Q} the reference and query FASTA files, \texttt{L} the minimum length and \texttt{T} the threads:

\begin{itemize}
  \item sporos: \texttt{sporos mem -maxmatch|-mum|-mumreference -l L -n -t T R Q}; capped: \texttt{sporos mem -maxmatch|-mum -b -{}-max-occ N -l 50 -t T R Q}; SMEMs: \texttt{sporos index -t T R}, then \texttt{sporos smem -l 19 -s f -t T R reads.fa}.
  \item MUMmer4: \texttt{mummer -maxmatch|-mum|-mumreference -n -l L R Q}. Its \texttt{-qthreads} divides only between query records, and \texttt{-threads} requires \texttt{-k} above 1, which aborted, so it ran on one thread.
  \item copMEM2: \texttt{copmem2 -q [-mf] -t T -l L -o out R Q}; \texttt{-t 10} did not change its time on a single query record.
  \item Mumemto: \texttt{mumemto -k 2 -f N -l 50} (per-genome cap) and \texttt{mumemto -k 2 -f 0 -F N -l 50} (total cap); MUMs: \texttt{mumemto -l L}.
  \item minibwa: \texttt{minibwa index -t T R prefix}, then \texttt{minibwa fastmap -l 19 -s f -b 64 prefix reads.fa} (batches of 64, its fastest setting).
  \item BWA: \texttt{bwa index}, then \texttt{bwa fastmap -l 19 index reads.fa}.
  \item ropebwt3: \texttt{ropebwt3 build -t T -do index.fmd R}, then \texttt{ropebwt3 mem -t T -l 19 -c f index.fmd reads.fa}.
  \item Minimizers and syncmers: \texttt{benchmarks/bench\_seeds.mojo} and \texttt{bench\_seeds\_fasta.mojo} (sporos), the \texttt{harness/smbench} program on simd-minimizers' packed sequences, and \texttt{harness/mm2} on minimap2's \texttt{mm\_sketch}.
  \item Seed lookups: \texttt{benchmarks/bench\_index.mojo} (sporos), \texttt{harness/lookup/mm2\_lookup.c} (minimap2's \texttt{mm\_sketch} and \texttt{mm\_idx\_get}) and \texttt{harness/lookup/sa\_bench} (strobealign's \texttt{randstrobes\_query} and \texttt{find\_hits}).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{MEMs and MUMs}

Tables S3 to S5 complete main Table 3: MEMs and MUMs of at least 100~bp, MEMs unique in the reference, and peak memory. copMEM2 takes at least 1.0~GB whatever the input size, and setting up its tables dominates its time on the small pair; sporos's anchor index grows with the reference and the sampling, and its peak on chromosome 1 at L = 50 comes from the 65.6 million MEMs it holds before filtering.

\section{SMEM outputs}

Table S7 compares the SMEMs of sporos with those of \texttt{bwa fastmap} and minibwa, by read, interval, number of occurrences and listed positions. Of the 5{,}242 SMEMs that only the other tool reports, 5{,}140 list a position whose reference span holds an N, which BWA and minibwa replace by random bases when they build their index and sporos never matches, and 0 list no positions, so that this check cannot tell; 102 remain. Ten threads gave the same output as one for every read set and f.
